-- The Lean grouping parser preserves inner semantic spans. A nomatch span
-- additionally covers its actually consumed tokens, including grouped scrutinees.
-- The input is the finite token list already constructed by the owned lexer.
def psLeanNomatchConsumedStop
    (tokens : List PsToken) :
    Option PsToken -> PsSourcePos -> PsSourcePos :=
  match tokens with
  | List.nil =>
      fun (_next : Option PsToken) (latest : PsSourcePos) => latest
  | List.cons token rest =>
      let smaller : Option PsToken -> PsSourcePos -> PsSourcePos :=
        psLeanNomatchConsumedStop rest;
      fun (next : Option PsToken) (latest : PsSourcePos) =>
        let finished : Bool :=
          if psTokenKindEq token.kind PsTokenKind.endOfInput then true
          else
            match next with
            | Option.none => false
            | Option.some unconsumed =>
                Nat.ble unconsumed.span.start.byteOffset token.span.start.byteOffset;
        if finished then latest
        else smaller next token.span.stop

def psParseLeanNomatch
    (parseScrutinee :
      PsTokenCursor ->
      Except PsParseError (PsParseResult PsSyntaxTerm))
    (cursor : PsTokenCursor) :
    Except PsParseError (PsParseResult PsSyntaxTerm) :=
  match psTokenCursorAdvance cursor with
  | Option.none => Except.error (PsParseError.unexpectedEnd "nomatch scrutinee")
  | Option.some keyword =>
      match parseScrutinee keyword.cursor with
      | Except.error error => Except.error error
      | Except.ok scrutinee =>
          let stop : PsSourcePos :=
            psLeanNomatchConsumedStop keyword.cursor.remaining
              (psTokenCursorPeek scrutinee.cursor) keyword.token.span.stop;
          Except.ok {
            value :=
              PsSyntaxTerm.matchE scrutinee.value List.nil {
                start := keyword.token.span.start
                stop := stop
              }
            cursor := scrutinee.cursor
          }

-- Each application family supplies its existing recursive parser here.
-- Grouped and list heads therefore retain that family's expression boundary.
def psParseLeanApplicationPrimary
    (parseNomatchScrutinee :
      PsTokenCursor ->
      Except PsParseError (PsParseResult PsSyntaxTerm))
    (parseParenthesized :
      PsTokenCursor ->
      Except PsParseError (PsParseResult PsSyntaxTerm))
    (cursor : PsTokenCursor) :
    Except PsParseError (PsParseResult PsSyntaxTerm) :=
  if psTokenCursorAtText cursor "nomatch" then
    psParseLeanNomatch parseNomatchScrutinee cursor
  else if psTokenCursorAtText cursor "(" then
    match psTokenCursorAdvance cursor with
    | Option.none => Except.error (PsParseError.unexpectedEnd "(")
    | Option.some opening =>
        if psTokenCursorAtText opening.cursor ")" then
          match psTokenCursorAdvance opening.cursor with
          | Option.none => Except.error (PsParseError.unexpectedEnd ")")
          | Option.some close =>
              Except.ok {
                value := PsSyntaxTerm.unit {
                  start := opening.token.span.start
                  stop := close.token.span.stop
                }
                cursor := close.cursor
              }
        else
          match parseParenthesized opening.cursor with
          | Except.error error => Except.error error
          | Except.ok inner =>
              match psTokenCursorExpectText inner.cursor ")" with
              | Except.error error => Except.error error
              | Except.ok close =>
                  Except.ok {
                    value := inner.value
                    cursor := close.cursor
                  }
  else if psTokenCursorAtText cursor "[" then
    match psTokenCursorAdvance cursor with
    | Option.none => Except.error (PsParseError.unexpectedEnd "[")
    | Option.some opening =>
        psParseLeanListLiteral parseParenthesized opening
  else
    psParseSimpleTerm cursor

def psParseLeanProductWithFuel
    (fuel : Nat) :
    PsTokenCursor ->
    Except PsParseError (PsParseResult PsSyntaxTerm) :=
  match fuel with
  | 0 =>
      fun (_cursor : PsTokenCursor) =>
        Except.error PsParseError.fuelExhausted
  | remaining + 1 =>
      let smaller :
          PsTokenCursor ->
          Except PsParseError (PsParseResult PsSyntaxTerm) :=
        psParseLeanProductWithFuel remaining;
      fun (cursor : PsTokenCursor) =>
        match
            psParseLeanApplicationWithFuel
              smaller
              (Nat.add remaining 1)
              cursor with
        | Except.error error => Except.error error
        | Except.ok left =>
            if psTokenCursorAtText left.cursor "×" then
              match psTokenCursorAdvance left.cursor with
              | Option.none =>
                  Except.error
                    (PsParseError.unexpectedEnd "product type")
              | Option.some afterProduct =>
                  match smaller afterProduct.cursor with
                  | Except.error error => Except.error error
                  | Except.ok right =>
                      let span :=
                        psSyntaxSpanJoin
                          (psSyntaxTermSpan left.value)
                          (psSyntaxTermSpan right.value);
                      let prodName : PsSyntaxName := {
                        segments :=
                          List.cons "Prod" List.nil
                        span := afterProduct.token.span
                      };
                      Except.ok {
                        value :=
                          PsSyntaxTerm.app
                            (PsSyntaxTerm.reference prodName)
                            (List.cons
                              left.value
                              (List.cons right.value List.nil))
                            span
                        cursor := right.cursor
                      }
            else
              Except.ok left

observedFailure.cause: The full Term fallback gave Product its own recursive parser for grouped/list application arguments. That path used psParseSimpleTerm at its head, bypassing the full Term nomatch dispatch.

sourceReview.sharedConstructor: psParseLeanNomatch calls the supplied scrutinee parser exactly once, builds matchE with List.nil alternatives, and uses the unchanged consumed-token stop helper. The existing full-term branch delegates to this helper with the same smaller full-term callback.
sourceReview.headDispatch: The new application primary recognizes nomatch, Unit/grouped heads and list heads, then falls back to the unchanged psParseSimpleTerm. The old psParseSimpleTerm head rejected leading '(' and '['. Accepting those heads is an intentional compositional closure needed for repeated parentheses and grouped/list nomatch scrutinees, and also admits their ordinary grouped/list-head counterparts. Grouped/list recursion uses the existing expression-family callback; grouped syntax preserves the inner semantic AST/span and advances past its own closing token. This does not give ordinary grouped if/let/fun/record forms an unrestricted full Term callback.
sourceReview.fullScrutineePlumbing: The internal product worker carries a Bool selector and an ordinary typed callback. The full Term fallback supplies true and its existing smaller full-term parser. Recursive product/group/list entries carry both unchanged; only a nomatch head uses the selected scrutinee callback. Ordinary grouped expressions still use the recursive Product parser.
sourceReview.standaloneEntries: All 75 pre-existing definition headers are byte-identical. Public ApplicationWithFuel passes its existing callback in both roles. Public ProductWithFuel uses false and the pre-existing psParseLeanSimpleApplication value; every false-mode recursive level selects its own smaller Product parser, so that supplied fallback is not invoked. These standalone entries retain their restriction on full control-form callbacks. The new primary intentionally closes existing grouping/list forms under nesting and can accept previously rejected grouped/list-head inputs; identical acceptance on all non-nomatch inputs is not claimed.
sourceReview.boundedFuel: No public fuel default or zero/successor behavior changes. Application tail, list and product recursion keep their existing counters. Product recursion decreases its own fuel. Each true-mode return to full Term uses the enclosing Term's already-decreased smaller callback; this decreases the enclosing Term fuel even after finite grouped/list product descent. No fuel retry, fresh token-count budget for nomatch, or unbounded recursion is added.
sourceReview.spans: The existing psLeanNomatchConsumedStop definition and comments are moved byte-identically. It stops before the next unconsumed token and includes consumed scrutinee parentheses. Parentheses surrounding the complete nomatch do not alter its semantic span. Lexer positions and UTF-8 byte offsets are unchanged.

authoringForms.declarationOrder: The moved span helper precedes shared nomatch; shared nomatch and primary precede the internal/public application workers; those precede SimpleApplication and the internal/public Product workers; full Term follows all of them. Every new referenced global is already declared.
authoringForms.callbackTypes: All new callback binders use the existing standalone typed-binder arrow form, matching existing parser callbacks. No Option of a grouped function-arrow type, type alias, new datatype, mutual definition, notation or unsupported binder syntax is introduced.
authoringForms.selectedParser: The if-valued parseScrutinee local has an explicit PsTokenCursor -> Except PsParseError (PsParseResult PsSyntaxTerm) type.
authoringForms.otherBindings: The span stop local has an explicit PsSourcePos type; moved helper lambdas have explicit parameter types; new branches return directly under the declared Except result. No new untyped lambda or match-valued unannotated local is introduced.
authoringForms.recursion: The internal Product worker structurally recurses on remaining fuel while the selector/callback parameters are unchanged. The full Term self-reference remains its already existing smaller binding. Public wrappers add no recursive call. The new primary is the intentional grouping/list compositional extension described above; no broader grouped function-arrow or full control callback capability is added.
